title: A Record 202.9M Shoppers Turned Out Thanksgiving Weekend

facts.fact: NRF reported that a record 202.9 million consumers shopped over the five-day holiday weekend from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday.
facts.quote: A record-breaking 202.9 million consumers shopped over the five-day holiday weekend from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday, according to the National Retail Federation (NRF).

facts.fact: According to NRF, the 2025 Thanksgiving weekend turnout exceeded the 197 million shoppers from the prior year.
facts.quote: This year’s turnout exceeded the 197 million shoppers last year and surpassed the previous record of 200.4 million set in 2023.

facts.fact: According to NRF, the previous record for Thanksgiving weekend shoppers of 200.4 million was set in 2023.
facts.quote: surpassed the previous record of 200.4 million set in 2023.

facts.fact: NRF's initial expectation for Thanksgiving weekend 2025 shoppers was 186.9 million, which the actual turnout beat.
facts.quote: It also beat the NRF’s initial expectations of 186.9 million shoppers over the holiday weekend.

facts.fact: According to the NRF survey, 134.9 million shoppers shopped online over the holiday weekend, up 9 percent year-over-year.
facts.quote: Online shopping was the most popular option, with 134.9 million shoppers, up 9 percent year-over-year

facts.fact: According to the NRF survey, 129.5 million consumers shopped in stores over the holiday weekend, up 3 percent year-over-year.
facts.quote: while 129.5 million consumers shopped in stores, up 3 percent year-over-year.

facts.fact: In-store shoppers on Black Friday totaled 80.3 million, below the 81.7 million in-store Black Friday shoppers last year, per NRF.
facts.quote: In-store shoppers totaled 80.3 million on Friday, below the 81.7 million shoppers last year

facts.fact: Online Black Friday shoppers totaled 85.7 million, below the 87.3 million online shoppers last year, per NRF.
facts.quote: while 85.7 million shopped online, below the 87.3 million last year.

facts.fact: In-store Small Business Saturday shoppers rose to 62.7 million from 61.1 million last year, per NRF.
facts.quote: Small Business Saturday drew more shoppers than last year, up to 62.7 million in-store compared with 61.1 million last year.

facts.fact: Online Small Business Saturday shoppers totaled 63 million, up from 53.9 million last year, per NRF.
facts.quote: Online shoppers totaled 63 million, up from 53.9 million last year.

facts.fact: The Sunday after Thanksgiving drew a record 32.6 million in-store shoppers, up from 25.6 million last year, per NRF.
facts.quote: The Sunday after Thanksgiving drew a record 32.6 million in-store shoppers, up from 25.6 million last year

facts.fact: On the Sunday after Thanksgiving, 38.7 million consumers shopped online, up from 32.8 million last year, per NRF.
facts.quote: while 38.7 million shopped online, up from 32.8 million last year.

facts.fact: Cyber Monday 2025 drew 75.9 million online shoppers, compared with 64.4 million in 2024, per NRF.
facts.quote: This Cyber Monday, there were 75.9 million online shoppers compared with 64.4 million in 2024.

facts.fact: Mobile was the most popular way for online shoppers to browse and buy on Cyber Monday, with 46.9 million consumers shopping on a mobile device, up from 40.4 million last year, per NRF.
facts.quote: with 46.9 million consumers shopping online on their mobile device, up from 40.4 million last year.

facts.fact: Cyber Monday celebrated its 20th anniversary in 2025.
facts.quote: Cyber Monday, which celebrates its 20th anniversary this year, was once again the second-most popular day for online shopping.

facts.fact: In the holiday weekend survey, supermarkets were the most-visited shopping location over Thanksgiving weekend at 47 percent, followed by online at 45 percent.
facts.quote: supermarkets took the top spot at 47 percent, followed by online (45 percent), department stores (40 percent)

facts.fact: In the holiday weekend survey, 40 percent of Thanksgiving weekend shoppers visited department stores, 37 percent visited clothing stores, and 30 percent visited discount stores.
facts.quote: department stores (40 percent), clothing stores (37 percent), and discount stores (30 percent).

facts.fact: In the holiday weekend survey, 96 percent of shoppers over Thanksgiving weekend made a holiday-related purchase.
facts.quote: Nearly everyone shopping over the weekend (96 percent) made a holiday-related purchase.

facts.fact: In the holiday weekend survey, 54 percent of shoppers took advantage of early deals and promotions over Thanksgiving weekend.
facts.quote: with 54 percent of shoppers taking advantage of early deals and promotions.

facts.fact: Holiday weekend shoppers spent an average of $337.86 on gifts, holiday apparel, decorations, and other seasonal purchases, up from $315.56 the prior year.
facts.quote: Shoppers spent $337.86 on average on gifts, holiday apparel, decorations, and other seasonal purchases, up from $315.56 last year

facts.fact: The $337.86 average holiday weekend spend is the highest since 2019's record average of $361.90 per the article's comparison.
facts.quote: marking the highest amount since 2019’s record of $361.90.

facts.fact: Of the money spent over the holiday weekend, 67 percent, or $225.74, was spent on gifts.
facts.quote: Of the money spent that weekend, 67 percent ($225.74) was spent on gifts.

facts.fact: The most popular gifts purchased over the holiday weekend were clothing and accessories at 51 percent, followed by toys at 32 percent, books and media at 28 percent, and gift cards at 26 percent.
facts.quote: clothing and accessories at 51 percent, followed by toys (32 percent), books and media (28 percent), and gift cards (26 percent).

facts.fact: As of Thanksgiving weekend, 84 percent of consumers said they had already begun their holiday shopping.
facts.quote: As of Thanksgiving weekend, 84 percent of consumers said they had already begun their holiday shopping.

facts.fact: As of Thanksgiving weekend, consumers said 53 percent of their holiday shopping remained to be done.
facts.quote: consumers stating they have more than half (53 percent) of their holiday shopping remaining.

facts.fact: The NRF defines the holiday season as November 1 through December 31.
facts.quote: The NRF, which defines the holiday season as Nov. 1 through Dec. 31

facts.fact: The NRF forecast that holiday spending will grow between 3.7 and 4.2 percent and exceed $1 trillion for the first time.
facts.quote: forecast last month that holiday spending will grow between 3.7 and 4.2 percent, exceeding $1 trillion for the first time.

facts.fact: The holiday weekend survey reached 3,099 adult consumers between Nov. 26 and Nov. 30.
facts.quote: The holiday weekend survey reached out to 3,099 adult consumers between Nov. 26-30.
